pages.text: The Jurassic was a middle time in dinosaur history. It came after the Triassic and before the Cretaceous. While dinosaurs spread, Earth itself was changing.
extras: Pangaea was starting to split apart.

images.alt: A map showing Earth during the Middle Jurassic, about 170 million years ago

pages.text: The Jurassic world was warm, with no ice caps. Ferns, tree ferns, conifers, ginkgos, cycads, and horsetails made green places for animals to live.
extras: There were no grass lawns yet.

images.alt: A Jurassic forest scene with dinosaurs among conifers and tree ferns

pages.text: Rivers and floodplains left layers of rock full of clues. In western North America, the Morrison Formation saved many Late Jurassic dinosaur fossils.
extras: Fossils are clues from deep time.

images.alt: Layered Morrison Formation rocks near Green River, Utah

pages.text: Brachiosaurus was a high browser. Its front legs were longer than its back legs, so its shoulders rose high like a living lookout tower.
extras: It could reach very high plants.

images.alt: A mounted Brachiosaurus skeleton showing its long neck and high shoulders

pages.text: Apatosaurus was another giant plant-eater. It walked on four sturdy legs, carried a long neck, and swung a long whip-like tail behind it.
extras: Its skull was small for its huge body.

images.alt: A restoration of Apatosaurus with a long neck and long tail

pages.text: Diplodocus was built long and low. Its tiny peg-like teeth sat near the front of its jaws, and its tail made up a huge part of its length.
extras: Some skeletons were about 24 to 26 meters long.

images.alt: A mounted Diplodocus skeleton with a very long neck and tail

pages.text: Stegosaurus wore tall plates along its back. Near the end of its tail were sharp spikes that probably helped protect it from hungry predators.

images.alt: A mounted Stegosaurus skeleton with upright back plates and tail spikes

pages.text: Stegosaurus was not built like a runner. It had a small head, a short neck, and a heavy plant-eating body balanced on four legs.
extras: Some grew more than 7 meters long.

images.alt: A Stegosaurus size chart comparing the dinosaur with a human

pages.text: Allosaurus was a big Jurassic hunter. It ran on two strong legs, balanced with a long tail, and had many sharp teeth for biting meat.
extras: It was a common large Morrison predator.

images.alt: A mounted Allosaurus skeleton showing its big skull, two legs, and long tail

pages.text: Allosaurus was large, but the giant plant-eaters were much larger. In Jurassic habitats, size could help protect a dinosaur from danger.
extras: Predator and prey lived in the same rocks.

images.alt: An Allosaurus size chart comparing the dinosaur with a human

pages.text: Near the end of the Jurassic, some small theropod dinosaurs were bird-like. Archaeopteryx had feathers and wings, but also teeth, claws, and a long bony tail.
extras: Every fossil is a piece of the story.

images.alt: The Berlin Archaeopteryx fossil showing bones and feather impressions
